title: Variant-aware GPU allocation and KV residency strategy for long-context models
creator: Amaya Chen
description: Problem: Long-context model configs (Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants, 32k+ tokens) push peak GPU memory into fragile regions when KV residency is conservative, causing OOMs or forced spill-to-host that spikes p99 latency. We need a per-variant strategy that: 1) allocates persistent GPU slab reservations tuned to model architecture and quantization; 2) manages KV residency using compacting windows and adaptive residency thresholds; 3) cooperates with continuous batching so eviction/compaction doesn't regress tail latency. Goal: reduce peak GPU memory by >=18% for quantized variants, keep p99 token latency regression <10%, and eliminate unplanned host spills in steady-state traffic.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Created: initial hypothesis and constraints captured. Noted heavy variance across models: Qwen-70B-long uses ~22% more KV overhead than Llama-2-70B-Long under same prompt shapes.

2025-02-20 - Experiment: ran baseline traces (internal perf bucket) with 64-concurrent sessions, 8k avg context. Observed peak GPU memory: Qwen-70B-q4_0 = 98.2 GB, Mistral-8x-Long = 45.7 GB, Llama-2-70B-Long = 92.1 GB.

2025-02-24 - Design decision: implement 'residency bands' -- three dynamic tiers (resident, hot-kv, warm-kv) with model-specific thresholds and a compacting window that runs on idle slices between batches. Rationale: avoids aggressive eviction during bursty events while still reclaiming memory during quiet periods.

2025-02-26 - Trade-offs: residency bands add metadata (per-shard counters) and add ~600 KB overhead per model shard. Benefit: reduces instantaneous eviction churn; Risk: complexity in testing rollout across Dedicated clusters.

2025-02-28 - Implementation update: landed KV residency tracker + compaction task skeleton. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2486 (WIP). Core work split: allocation policy (Diego), compaction engine (Amaya), compat shim with continuous-batcher (Nora).

2025-03-01 - Benchmark round 1: enabled residency bands + model-aware slab sizing. Results vs baseline: peak mem down by 20% on Qwen-70B-q4_0 (98.2 -> 78.6 GB), 18% on Llama-2-70B-Long, 14% on Mistral-8x-Long. p50 token latency unchanged, p99 latency increased by ~6% under synthetic burst test. No host spill events observed in 2h soak.

2025-03-02 - Review feedback from SRE: add observability metrics (residency_ratio, compaction_cycles, avg_eviction_per_min) and alarms for compaction backlog > 3. Also suggested a canary rollout on dedicated-early region before global rollout.

2025-03-03 - Follow-ups: tuning plan documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Variant+Residency+Strategy. Added integration tests to catch regression where continuous-batcher merges requests immediately after compaction leading to a 50ms stall.

2025-03-04 - Next steps: finish PR reviews, add dashboards (Grafana) for new metrics, run 24hr soak on dedicated-canary with real traffic traces, prepare rollback plan (feature flag + force-evict policy) and update runbook for on-call.

Implementation notes: use model heuristics derived from offline profiling (context length distribution, kv-token density, quantization factor). Default heuristics: q4_0 models get +10% resident slab to avoid recompute; long-context variants (>=32k) use longer compacting window (500ms idle) to reduce churn.
Open questions: whether to expose a per-customer tuning knob in Dedicated for aggressive residency vs cost optimization, and whether to persist recent KV residency heatmaps to speed cold restarts.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated, canary to dedicated-early (2 nodes) for 48h -> extend to 10% fleet for 72h -> full rollout. Metrics gating: no host spills, peak mem reduction >=15% on canary, p99 token latency regression <10% compared to baseline.
